title: GTH Algorithm, Censored Markov Chains, and $RG$-Factorization in Block-Form
summary: In 1985, Grassmann, Taksar, and Heyman published their celebrated paper, in which they introduced a numerically stable algorithm for computing the stationary probabilities of a finite-state Markov chain, one of the key performance quantities in both theory and applications. This algorithm later became the well-known GTH algorithm (or the state-reduction method) in the literature, becoming one of the standard algorithms in applied probability. Later, this algorithm was extended to deal with the stationary distributions of block-structured Markov chains with repeating rows. In this paper, we…
